article.title: HC Ajoie signs forward Logan Brown
article.description: The 28-year-old forward has signed a contract through the end of 2026—including an option to extend through the end of the season.
article.text:
HC Ajoie has announced the signing of Logan Brown as its seventh import player. The American-Canadian dual citizen has signed a contract running through the end of 2026, which includes an option for the remainder of the season. Brown played for the Ontario Reign in the AHL last season and has been a free agent since the end of last season.

The 28-year-old can play both on the wing and at center. He was drafted 11th overall in the first round by the Ottawa Senators in 2016. He has spent most of his career so far in the AHL; in the NHL, he has played 99 games (26 points) for the Senators and the St. Louis Blues.

According to a club statement, Brown will arrive in Porrentruy in the coming days and will be eligible to play as soon as the final formalities are settled.

article.title: Interest from Switzerland in Rögle's Dan Tangnes
article.description: The Norwegian coach with a Swiss past is reportedly drawing the attention of some National League clubs.
article.text:
Dan Tangnes left Switzerland a bit over a year ago, when he joined Rögle BK. Prior to that, he was EV Zug's head coach for seven seasons (winning the championship twice and the cup once). As the "Helsingborgs Dagblad" (relayed by "Hockeynews.se") writes, there appears to be interest from some Swiss clubs in the Norwegian. His contract with Rögle expires in 2028.

"I am glad there is interest from other places, but there have not been any discussions or anything concrete to consider", Tangnes is cited by the "Dagblad".

Rögle, currently sitting in the middle of the SHL's standings with 14 points from ten games (tied with four other teams), would like to extend with their head coach.

article.title: Yannick Rathgeb will likely play tonight
article.description: As the Freiburger Nachrichten report, the 30-year-old defenseman missed practice on Thursday.
article.text:
According to head coach Roger Rönnberg, Yannick Rathgeb should, however, be able to play tonight, as he is only dealing with minor muscular problems.

Samuel Walser and Jonas Taibel, on the other hand, will likely not return to HC Fribourg-Gottéron's lineup, but at least Walser should soon be ready to play again and is expected to make his comeback next week.

article.title: Mirco Müller in, Jesper Peltonen and Alessio Bertaggia out for Lugano
article.description: While one defenseman returns, another one plus a forward are expected to be sidelined for about a month.
article.text:
Tuesday's game against Genève-Servette HC may have been successful score-wise for HC Lugano, but personnel-wise, it was rather unfortunate. Alessio Bertaggia suffered a lower-body injury in warm-up, while Jesper Peltonen injured his left arm during the game and had to toss the towel early. As RSI writes, both are expected to be out for about a month.

On a more positive note, Mirco Müller, who missed Tuesday's game, is ready to go again for the weekend. Lorenzo Canonica, Carl Dahlström, and Dario Simion, however, are still sidelined.

article.title: HC Ajoie's Daniel Carr suspended for five games
article.description: Having already served one, the Canadian forward will miss the next four games of the Ajoulots.
article.text:
Daniel Carr has been suspended for five games and fined CHF 7'600 for punching EHC Biel's Gaëtan Haas in the head when he was kneeling on the ice after a fight between the two players on Friday. Haas suffered a concussion due to the punch and is now sidelined indefinitely.

The Single Judge, Karl Knopf, deliberated that the action of the Canadian was to be considered a sucker punch and therefore a category III offense (the highest level, minimum five games of suspension). Within the category, Knopf opted for the lightest sentence, as Haas had just been engaged in the fight with Carr and was thus not hit out of nowhere.

The full explanation of Knopf's decision can be found here, while the video of the action can be found here.

article.title: EHC Biel without Haas and Iakovenko until further notice
article.description: The Seelanders already had to make do without the two players in Saturday's game.
article.text:
Gaëtan Haas was punched by Daniel Carr in the game between HC Ajoie and EHC Biel on Friday. The 34-year-old suffered a concussion and will be out of the lineup until further notice. Watson had already reported that Haas was going to miss the game against the SC Rapperswil-Jona Lakers on Tuesday.

Apart from Haas, EHC Biel will also have to make do without Aleksandr Iakovenko. The 28-year-old defenseman is dealing with a torn muscle and is considered week-to-week.
